issue_context.title: Implement chunking for gzip encoder in `deferredResponseWriter`
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As pointed out in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129334#discussion_r1938405782 existing implementation of [deferredResponseWriter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b4f902f0371485505ff4eda39975e67bfa9b0727/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/responsewriters/writers.go#L190-L200) assumes a single write when deciding whether gzip encoding is needed. We would extend writes to allow multiple calls to `Write`.

To support multiple calls to `Write` and still make an accurate decision about whether to enable `gzip` encoding, we will need to buffer the response until its size reach the gzip threshold `defaultGzipThresholdBytes` or `Close` is called. At that point we can flush the buffer as it's no longer needed.


As a prerequisite to this change we developed a test to validate the current chunking behavior in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130190. As part of this PR we want to flip `expectGzip` flag to true as part of `"two small chunk writes"` scenario. Context https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130190#discussion_r1960338824

### Why is this needed?

Required to implement response streaming described in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/5116-streaming-response-encoding#streaming-collections-and-gzip-encoding

Tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5116

review_comments:
@wojtek-t @serathius are we concerned that this is doubling allocations for write paths that are gzip-enabled, are smaller than defaultGzipThresholdBytes, and won't do multiple writes? that includes *all* single-object writes and *all* non-streaming list writes (which will be the majority of list writes until we implement streaming list for json and proto and those features enable)

do we want to try to indicate to the deferredResponseWriter whether we expect multiple Write calls so it can avoid this cost when we don't expect to Write multiple times?

Even if we implement streaming for JSON, Writing Get/Put/Post response is always done in single write.  However I don't think it should impact whole apiserver much. All those requests are served from etcd, this already requires at least 2 allocations to read from etcd. For lists served from cache, they are still much cheaper than ones from etcd.
Wait a sec, for single write case, could we just store the first write and not append?

I don't think we can / should... from https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer:

> Implementations must not retain p.
Right

Those additional allocations shouldn't make a visible difference (it should mostly be one additional allocation per single-object call, which doesn't sound that bad - the performance of allocations was improved tremendously around go1.16 or sth like that).

Though, if we can somehow avoid it without introducing too much complexity, then it would be good to avoid it.
yeah, I think we found a clean way to limit the buffering to our streaming list cases

We might want to do benchmarks on the chunking. When working on streaming I already have prepared a benchmark, It might be useful here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/e44db267542250ef7ca3f9954ed93841e12c03f5

@z1cheng could you look into benchmarking gzip with and without chunking for different sizes of objects and number like in the linked commit?

> @z1cheng could you look into benchmarking gzip with and without chunking for different sizes of objects and number like in the linked commit?

Sure, let me try

> @liggitt do you think we need a buffer pooling here? Do you know why we do gzip pooling?

it was to avoid allocation churn and reuse the gzip writers

a buffer pool is not a bad idea... if we're going to be retaining these, ideally our pooled buffers would not grow saved buffers past defaultGzipThresholdBytes+1, but that would require slightly trickier buffer accumulation logic in this function

```
w.buffer = append(w.buffer, p...)
```

Based on #129334, first several writes might be way smaller than `defaultGzipThresholdBytes`. 
before marshaling metadata field, it has been resized 3 times, even if it's small size. Pre-allocation could be good here.

```
T0: write `{`            // buffer cap: 8
T1: write `"kind"`       // buffer cap: 8
T2: write `:`            // buffer cap: 8
T3: write `"pods"`       // buffer cap: 16
T4: write `,`            // buffer cap: 16
T5: write `"apiversion"` // buffer cap: 32
T6: write `":"`          // buffer cap: 32
T7: write `"v1"`         // buffer cap: 32
T8: write `","`          // buffer cap: 64
T9: write ....
```

I was considering using a `[][]byte` tracker for each write before gzip to reduce copying.
Pre-allocating `[][]byte` with a size of 128 should be sufficient, as it's smaller than `defaultGzipThresholdBytes + 1`.

However, in the HTTP/2 layer, this approach requires additional cycles to send `defaultGzipThresholdBytes`. Each write results in a FrameWriteRequest, and for the initial writes, each request contains a small dataset. The HTTP/2 layer processes only one FrameWriteRequest at a time, even if it's smaller than the window size.

If we can buffer the first several writes into a larger buffer, we could improve efficiency by reducing the number of small requests.

https://cs.opensource.google/go/x/net/+/refs/tags/v0.35.0:http2/writesched.go;drc=120fc906b30bade8c220769da77801566d7f4ec8;l=106

I think we should pick just a simple solution for now to unblock other work, and revisit the issue in separate PR. 
Either skip preallocation or preallocate just minimal number of characters that always are needed.

For how big a minimal preallocation would be I think minimal JSON response has around 80 characters `{\"kind\":\"List\",\"apiVersion\":\"v1\",\"metadata\":{\"resourceVersion\":\"1\"},\"items\":[]}\n`
I think we can just put 80 and document where the number comes from.

Preallocating larger size like deferredResponseWriter would require a performance measurements and consideration whether we want to reuse the buffer. Don't think we should block on it.
add a comment here explaining that we never reached the gzip writer minimum size, so we can return without needing to do the gzip writer cleanup
returning here is not correct... we want to write the buffer and then attempt to close... if this passed tests then we need a test covering this bug
(calling unbufferedWrite will flip hasWritten from false to true)

When `hasWritten` is false and `hasBuffered` is true, it means the buffer has not reached the `defaultGzipThresholdBytes`. So `unbufferedWrite` won't use the gzip writer, and there is no need to close the gzip writer, we can just return directly.
ah, Close() was only doing something in the gzip case... I thought it was passing through to call w.w.Close() in all cases
I just realized `io.Writer` doesn't even provide the Close()
Maybe we should set Body to nil so that it won't store the data in cache. (discard the data)
